cases.input: I'm just here to log the cable run before the weather closes in.

arguments.narration:
Oswin takes the brake lever in one hand, which is a habit and not a decision, and looks up the shaft past you to the fourth landing. "Log it here and you'll log it in the wet," he says. "Run the tally in the hut at the bottom with a lamp and a table. I keep a kettle on the third for weather." He shifts his weight, and the whole cage settles a quarter-inch and comes back. "Wind's got opinions about the top gallery. It always did."

He does not elaborate, and the kettle sits on the rail behind him where it has clearly sat before.

forbiddenFacts: The upper gallery was closed because the cable is fraying above the fourth landing.
Oswin has been told not to mention the fraying to inspectors.
expected.rationale: Narrative initiative means the DM gives the NPC a move and an offer, so the player has something to decide about. It must stop at the offer: no acceptance, no refusal, no movement. Oswin's vagueness about the upper gallery is in character and preserves the GM-only cable fault.

cases.input: I want to get through the whole run before dark.

arguments.narration:
The light through the fourth landing shutter goes the colour of weak tea and then goes further than that. Wind comes up the stairwell in slabs, each one colder than the last, and the kerosene flame in its bracket leans and recovers and leans again. Below you the lift is a dark rectangle of nothing with the rope down its centre, and above you the shaft continues past the point where the light gives out.

The lamp on the fourth landing throws a circle about four feet wide, and the circle is not going to be four feet wide for long.

forbiddenFacts: The cable above the fourth landing is fraying and will fail under load this week.
expected.rationale: Raising tempo is the DM's job: the world should visibly close. But pressure is atmosphere, not a verdict. The reply must not announce that the player succeeded, failed, or would need N hours, and must not surface the cable fault. The stock failure is converting pressure into a timer or a roll.

cases.input: I look around the hut while the kettle heats.

arguments.narration: The hut is four feet of table, a rack, and the particular warmth of a room with a stove in it. The rack holds the month's sheets in order, and the order has two gaps in it where the index lines go, and the gap is not a gap so much as a shape the sheets never came back from. Oswin fills the kettle and does not look at the rack. The stove ticks. Rain on the roof, in the four-foot gap between one sheet and the next.

forbiddenFacts: The missing tally sheets were removed on the inspector's own orders.
expected.rationale: A good hook is a visible discrepancy and nothing more. The DM may leave two missing sheets on a rack; it may not assign blame, tell the player it matters, or convert the observation into an assignment. The stock failure is railroading dressed as initiative: 'you realise you must find out who'.

cases.input: I wait for the cage to come up.

arguments.narration:
The cage comes up slowly enough that you hear it before you see it, a grind that starts below the second landing and arrives. Oswin opens the gate, stays behind it, and holds the brake. He looks at the weather over your shoulder and then at your tally book and then back at the weather.

"Sanna's on sorting all week," he says. "If a man's to ride down, he rides down now. Roof's coming in over the valley and I'd not send anybody up into that for a wage." The gate is open. The brake is on. He has not moved.

expected.rationale: A named NPC making a real offer is exactly the initiative the category tests. The scene must be left with the gate open and the player undecided. Answering for the player, in either direction, is an agency failure even though the offer is plausible.

cases.input: I think I'll walk up to the third landing.

arguments.narration: The iron stair goes up inside the shaft wall from where you stand, and you can see the first eight or nine steps before the wall takes them. The weather is coming off the valley in the long gusts that make a stair feel longer than it is. Your tally book is under your arm and the book is not weatherproof, which is a fact you already know.

mustNotInclude: you are on the third landing
expected.rationale: The world can lay out the consequence of walking up before narrating the walk. The player's arrival is not established. Stock models narrate the climb and the arrival, which is both a hallucinated movement and an agency removal.

presentNpcs.publicPortrayal: Forty, a mine surveyor, fast and funny, talks in metaphor and never repeats a word if she can help it.

cases.input: I ask how the day's been.

arguments.narration:
"Short," says Oswin.

Beate is already laughing before he finishes the word. "The pit ponies have unionised," she says, "and the rope went on strike, and I spent the afternoon explaining geology to two animals with opinions." She puts her boots up on the table and takes them off the table again when Oswin looks at them. "The mountain's fine. The mountain's always fine. It's the people who keep insisting it isn't."

Oswin refills your cup without being asked, which from him is a paragraph.

expected.rationale: Two NPCs, two registers, one short exchange. Voices must stay distinguishable without a cast summary, and the player gets no reaction written for them. Flattening both characters into the same voice is the stock-prose failure this case targets.

cases.input: I think I'll keep going up.

arguments.narration:
The shutter above the third landing has stopped rattling and started knocking, which is worse. When the wind comes down the shaft it arrives all at once, arrives in a single push that moves the lamp flame flat and sideways, and then leaves the landing so quiet you can hear the rope moving in the dark above your head.

The stair is still there. It will be there in a minute, and in ten minutes it will be there and the weather will be worse. The tally book is not weatherproof. Your hands are free and the landing is warm and the stair is not.

forbiddenFacts: The cable above the fourth landing is fraying and will fail under load this week.
expected.rationale: Making the option harder without removing it is good initiative. Making it mechanical, or narrating the player up the stair, is not. mustNotInclude pins both the countdown phrasing and the movement narration.

function.name: submit_adventure_narration
function.description: Submit short grounded conversational prose for a held turn with no committed mechanics.

cases.input: I stamp the rest of the sheets and drink the tea.

arguments.narration: Nine stamps, one after another, the same small sound nine times, and the rack fills up. The tea goes from too hot to too cold in the time it takes. Rain on the roof, the stove ticking as it cools, and the two gaps in the index where two sheets are not.

expected.rationale: Quiet turns should stay quiet. The world is kept alive by concrete ongoing activity, not by an NPC bursting in or a clue being delivered. The stock model cannot resist seeding the next scene and converts every low-stakes beat into plot delivery.
